_comment: Explanatory-depth corpus schema v1. Implements Architectural Charter section 11 (Liturgical Education Layer), which makes educational explanation a first-class architectural layer with three depths. One file per tradition -- NOT one shared file -- per UNIVERSAL_OFFICE_CORE_CONTRACT.md section 2 (non-flattening rule) and section 3 (resolver separation). No tradition's explanatory content may be written from another tradition's.

tradition.note: Tradition code, matching data/horologion/schema.json's traditionCodes: ANG, COE, BYZC, ETH, LAT. Coptic uses OOR-COP.

traditionLabel.note: Human-readable tradition label as shown to the user.

primarySource.note: The governing source edition for this file's explanatory content. Every entry's own `source` cites a specific page within it (or names a different source explicitly).

sourceStatus.note: Honest statement of whether the governing source is actually held in this repository. 'unsourced' files must carry only nulls.

entries.note: Map of explanation key -> entry. See entryShape.

traditionExplanationShape._comment: DEPTH 3 -- Charter section 11.3: 'broader comparative explanation answering how does this tradition work, and how does it differ from others?'

text.note: null when not yet sourced. Null-sentinel per Charter section 13: the resolver treats null as 'not yet written' and the UI shows nothing, never a placeholder or a guess.

source.note: Specific page citation. Required whenever `text` is non-null.

label.note: The lane-native name of this element. Per Core Contract section 6, the shell shows the lane's own label and does not translate it.

role.note: From the shared block role taxonomy, UNIVERSAL_OFFICE_CORE_CONTRACT.md section 7. Closed by governance -- a lane may not invent a role. Structural category only; never encodes rank, season, or theology.

matchLabels.note: Rendered label strings that resolve to this entry. Matching is case-insensitive on the normalized label text emitted inside <span class='rubric-text'>. This is how the layer attaches without rewriting the renderers' string building.

micro.note: DEPTH 1 -- Charter section 11.1: 'short tooltip or inline gloss answering what is this?'. One or two sentences. null = not yet sourced.

structural.note: DEPTH 2 -- Charter section 11.2: 'short expandable explanation answering how does this fit into the office?'. A short paragraph. null = not yet sourced.

source.note: Specific page citation for this entry's content. Required whenever `micro` or `structural` is non-null. An entry with content and no source is a governance violation.

rules: Nothing in this corpus may be written from memory. Every non-null string is written from a source read directly, and cites the page it was read from.
null is the correct value for anything not yet sourced. The resolver renders nothing for null -- it never substitutes a placeholder, a guess, or another tradition's explanation.
Explanatory content must preserve tradition-specific logic and must not flatten distinctions between traditions for convenience (Charter section 11, final clause).
The `role` field exists so the shell can treat structurally similar parts consistently. It is never a licence to reuse one tradition's explanation for another tradition's element.
Adding a tradition file whose governing source is not held requires sourceStatus 'unsourced' or 'cited-not-in-repo' and all-null content until the source is actually read.
